title: Havok collision material in Fallout 4 NIFs: the ID is a CRC32 of the MATT record name (Stone, Metal, Wood...)
content:
Havok collision material in Fallout 4 NIFs: the ID is a CRC32 of the MATT record name (Stone, Metal, Wood...)
The footstep, bullet-impact and debris effects of a collision come from its Havok material. In Fallout 4 the material is not a fixed list as in Skyrim: it is the ID of a MATT (Material Type) record in Fallout4.esm (147 of them). The ID is Bethesda's CRC32 of the record's name in lower case. In Python: zlib.crc32(name.lower().encode(), 0xFFFFFFFF) ^ 0xFFFFFFFF.
Common values:
- Stone 0xDF02F237
- Metal 0x064003D4
- Wood 0x1DD9C611
- Plastic 0x7DFA6E05
Where the ID sits in the NIF: convex, compound, capsule and sphere shapes keep it in the hknpShape userData at offset +0x18 (64-bit, the upper half is always 0). Compressed (exact-mesh) collision keeps it in hknpBSMaterialProperties at +0x34.
What vanilla uses: rocks use Stone, trees use Wood, plants use Grass, actors use the Actor materials (ActorSkin, ActorMetal and so on).
Common mistakes:
- Skyrim material names such as HEAVY_STONE, LIGHT_WOOD or SOLID_METAL are not Fallout 4 materials. Only Stone, Wood, Grass, Glass, Cloth, Organic, Skin and Dirt exist in both games under the same name.
- PyNifly's collision template always writes Plastic, so a rock exported without changing it rings like plastic when shot.
The Mossy Blender add-on (5.4.7 and later) writes the real ID of the material you pick.

verified_by: MATT record names in Fallout4.esm hashed and matched against the material IDs read from vanilla collision NIFs in the unpacked game, 2026-11-04; the four CRC values recomputed 2026-11-05.

title: Fallout 4 NIF basics that differ from Skyrim: header version 20.2.0.7 / 12 / 130, NiNode root, BSXFlags 130 with collision
content:
Fallout 4 NIF basics that differ from Skyrim: header version 20.2.0.7 / 12 / 130, NiNode root, BSXFlags 130 with collision
Checked against every NIF in the unpacked vanilla game:
- Header: NIF version 20.2.0.7, user version 12, Bethesda stream version 130. Stream 83 or 100 means a Skyrim file, which Fallout 4 will not load correctly.
- The root node is a NiNode. BSFadeNode roots are Skyrim's.
- Every vanilla shape has a shader property (13,024 of 13,024 files). A shape without one renders wrongly or not at all.
- BSXFlags: vanilla NIFs with collision have a BSXFlags extra data of 130 on the root. NIFs without collision (many statics, architecture pieces and plants) have no BSXFlags at all.
- One BSTriShape can hold at most 65,535 vertices, because the triangles use 16-bit vertex numbers. Vertices split at UV seams and hard edges count too, so the number in the NIF is higher than Blender's vertex count. Split larger meshes into several shapes.
tags: nif version 20.2.0.7 user version 12 stream 130 83 skyrim nif header ninode bsfadenode root node bsxflags 130 collision shader property bstrishape vertex limit 65535
verified_by: Scan of the NIFs in the unpacked vanilla Fallout 4 Data folder (header versions, root node types, shader count 13,024 of 13,024, BSXFlags with and without collision), 2026-11-04.

title: Fallout 4 normal maps are DirectX style (green channel down): fixing bumps that look like dents
content:
Fallout 4 normal maps are DirectX style (green channel down): fixing bumps that look like dents
Fallout 4 tangent-space normal maps use the DirectX convention: the green channel points down the image (often written Y- or -Y). Blender bakes and glTF / GLB files (most AI mesh generators) use the OpenGL convention (Y+). An OpenGL map in Fallout 4 looks lit from the wrong side: bumps look like dents and edges catch light from below.
Fixes:
- Baking in Blender: Bake type Normal, Swizzle G set to -Y (in Python: bake normal_g = 'NEG_Y').
- An existing OpenGL map: invert the green channel in an image editor (or in Paint.NET / GIMP / Photoshop), then convert to DDS.
- Substance Painter: export with the DirectX normal map setting.
Note: in Fallout 4 NIFs Bethesda's "bitangent" runs along U and "tangent" along V, the other way round from the usual names, so a tool that swaps them still looks right.
The Mossy Blender add-on's bakes (Retopologize & Bake, Re-bake from Source) bake the DirectX way.
tags: normal map directx opengl green channel inverted flipped -y y- bumps look like dents lit from below normal_g neg_y swizzle gltf substance painter bake normal
verified_by: Tangent frames stored in 7 of 7 vanilla NIFs checked (V vector along +V in top-left UV space, i.e. DirectX), 2026-11-04; Blender 5.1 bakes with normal_g NEG_Y compared.

title: Hard edges look smooth and rounded in game after exporting a NIF from Blender (one normal per NIF vertex)
content:
Hard edges look smooth and rounded in game after exporting a NIF from Blender (one normal per NIF vertex)
A NIF vertex can hold only one normal. Vanilla meshes therefore duplicate vertices along every hard edge, so each side of the edge gets its own normal. Blender keeps one vertex and gives each face corner its own normal (sharp edges, flat shading, custom split normals). PyNifly splits vertices only at UV seams, so on export the corner normals of one vertex are averaged: flat panels look bent, sharp edges look rounded and smeared.
Fixes:
- Mossy Blender add-on 5.4.8 or later: export splits a temporary copy along every hard edge, as vanilla does. Your mesh in Blender is not changed.
- By hand: on a copy, add an Edge Split modifier (Sharp Edges on) and apply it, or mark the edges as seams.
A second cause: Merge by Distance (remove doubles) before export merges the duplicated vertices of an imported vanilla mesh and destroys its hard edges. The add-on (5.4.8) keeps those normals as custom normals when it merges.
Measured: a re-exported vanilla ammo box lid had 293 wrong normals out of 422 before the fix and none after.
Every split vertex counts towards the 65,535-vertex limit of a shape.
tags: hard edges smooth rounded shading wrong in game normals smeared flat shading custom split normals sharp edges export nif pynifly edge split merge by distance remove doubles vertex normal
verified_by: Vanilla ammo box lid imported and re-exported in Blender 5.1 with PyNifly, per-vertex normals compared with the original NIF: 293/422 wrong before, 0 after (2026-11-05).

title: Armor and clothing SSF segment file path: must be relative to Data, not a full C:\ path
content:
Armor and clothing SSF segment file path: must be relative to Data, not a full C:\ path
Armor and clothing NIFs point to an .ssf segment file (used for dismemberment and body-part damage). Vanilla NIFs always store this path relative to the Data folder (1,667 of 1,667 files). A full disk path such as C:\Users\...\MyArmor.ssf only works on the PC that made it.
PyNifly writes the path relative only when the NIF is saved somewhere inside a folder named Meshes. Exported anywhere else, it writes the full disk path.
Fix: export into a Meshes folder of a mod folder structure (for example Downloads\MyMod\Meshes\MyArmor\), or correct the path in NifSkope. The Mossy Blender add-on (5.4.7 and later) warns when the path would come out absolute.

verified_by: All 1,667 vanilla NIFs that name an SSF file checked (all Data-relative); PyNifly export to a folder with and without Meshes in its path compared, 2026-11-04.

title: How sharp should Fallout 4 textures be? Vanilla texel density per category (pixels per metre)
content:
How sharp should Fallout 4 textures be? Vanilla texel density per category (pixels per metre)
Texel density is how many texture pixels cover one metre of surface. Matching vanilla keeps a new item from looking blurry or oddly sharp next to vanilla ones. Measured from the unpacked game, 40 meshes per category (median, with the middle half in brackets), counting 70 game units per metre:
- Weapons: 4,323 px/m (2,846 to 9,230)
- Clothes: 3,057 px/m (2,159 to 3,799)
- Armor: 2,659 px/m (2,084 to 3,338)
- Creatures: 2,536 px/m (1,082 to 2,578)
- Furniture: 1,019 px/m (562 to 1,869)
- Plants: 976 px/m (511 to 1,976)
- Props and clutter: 709 px/m (490 to 1,120)
- Architecture: 544 px/m (280 to 649)
- Rocks: 358 px/m (337 to 670)
Example: a prop whose UVs fill a 1024 texture should have about 1.4 m of surface across it. A 1 m wide weapon part needs about 4,000 pixels across, which is why weapons share one large texture between many parts.
The Mossy Blender add-on's UV & Texture Kit (Texture Helpers > UV & Texture Kit) measures a mesh's density against these values and can scale the UV islands to match.
tags: texel density texture resolution how big texture size pixels per metre blurry texture too sharp weapons armor clothes props architecture rocks plants furniture creatures 1024 2048 4096
verified_by: Median of 40 vanilla meshes per category: each shape's UV area times its real diffuse DDS size, over its surface area at 70 units per metre (unpacked Fallout 4, 2026-11-04).

title: Turning an AI-generated or very high-detail mesh (Meshy, Tripo, photogrammetry) into a Fallout 4 game mesh
content:
Turning an AI-generated or very high-detail mesh (Meshy, Tripo, photogrammetry) into a Fallout 4 game mesh
AI-generated and scanned meshes usually have far too many triangles, holes, hundreds of loose scraps, pieces passing through each other, and OpenGL normal maps. They cannot be exported as they are. The workflow that worked in tests:
1. Keep the highest-detail version you have as the source. The rebuild loses detail, and the bake can only bring back detail that is still in the source.
2. Rebuild a clean low-poly mesh around it. For broken meshes, first wrap everything in one closed skin, then remesh to quads (QuadriFlow) and reduce to your triangle budget.
3. Unwrap with as few, as big UV islands as possible.
4. Bake the colour and a DirectX normal map from the source onto the new mesh.
5. Then materials, collision, and export as usual.
In the Mossy Blender add-on (5.4.8): select the source and click Mesh Helpers > Mesh Shaper > Retopology > Retopologize & Bake. It does steps 2 to 4 and reports what it did.
Results on real AI meshes (Blender 5.1, 2026-11-05): a root cluster came out at 13,400 triangles with 28 UV islands, two of which hold 99% of the surface; a flower at 7,600 triangles kept its small petals.
Limit: very thin, tangled strands (vines, wires, hair) fuse together when rebuilt automatically. Rebuild those by hand (RetopoFlow, a free GPL add-on) or replace them with alpha-tested cards, as vanilla foliage does.
tags: ai generated mesh meshy tripo photogrammetry scan high poly low poly retopology retopo game ready fallout 4 too many triangles holes loose pieces bake normal map quadriflow remesh retopoflow vines
verified_by: Retopologize & Bake run in Blender 5.1 on AI-generated meshes 2026-11-05 (roots, flower, vine column): triangle counts, island counts and petal shape checked by rendering; the vine column fused at 33,500 triangles.

title: UV unwrapping for repainting textures: fewest and biggest UV islands, drape unwrap, and re-baking after the UVs change
content:
UV unwrapping for repainting textures: fewest and biggest UV islands, drape unwrap, and re-baking after the UVs change
Fewer, bigger UV islands make a texture much easier to repaint: brush strokes and patterns run across the surface instead of breaking at every seam. Blender's Smart UV Project does the opposite (many small islands).
In the Mossy Blender add-on (Texture Helpers > UV & Texture Kit):
- Auto Unwrap, Fewest Islands style: cuts the fewest seams, hidden underneath or at the back, that let the mesh lie flat. A part that would be squeezed or blown up (a fin on a body) becomes its own island.
- Auto Unwrap, Hard Surface style: seams along hard edges and material borders, for weapons and props.
- Drape Unwrap: two islands, as if a sheet were laid over the mesh from each side (Top / Bottom, Front / Back, Right / Left, or Auto). Touch Up Problem Areas moves faces that would streak or share texture into their own strip.
Read the report: if it says faces could not be unwrapped (squashed flat), the mesh is broken there (pieces passing through each other). Clean it up or rebuild it first.
Re-unwrapping moves the islands, so any texture painted or baked for the old UVs no longer lines up. Bake again from the high-detail source (select the source, then the game mesh last, then Mesh Shaper > Retopology > Re-bake from Source) or repaint.

title: Blender QuadriFlow remesh silently does nothing from a script: its real settings and the CANCELLED result
content:
Blender QuadriFlow remesh silently does nothing from a script: its real settings and the CANCELLED result
bpy.ops.object.quadriflow_remesh in Blender 5.1 takes exactly these settings: use_mesh_symmetry, use_preserve_sharp, use_preserve_boundary, preserve_attributes, smooth_normals, mode, target_ratio, target_edge_length, target_faces, mesh_area, seed.
Two traps:
- Any other keyword (for example use_mesh_curvature) raises an error. Code that catches errors and falls back to another remesh then never runs QuadriFlow at all, without telling you. This hid a bug in the Mossy Blender add-on until 5.4.8.
- When QuadriFlow refuses a mesh (holes, non-manifold edges, overlapping parts) it returns {'CANCELLED'} instead of raising. Always check the result: if 'FINISHED' not in result, it failed.
Give it one closed, clean mesh: remove loose scraps, recalculate normals, fill holes. Even so it can refuse meshes made by a voxel or SDF skin; then a voxel remesh plus Decimate is the fallback.

title: Mossy Blender add-on 5.4.8 mesh tools: Mesh Shaper (unbevel, booleans, normals) and where to get RetopoFlow safely
content:
Mossy Blender add-on 5.4.8 mesh tools: Mesh Shaper (unbevel, booleans, normals) and where to get RetopoFlow safely
Fallout 4 > Mesh Helpers > Mesh Shaper, for weapons, props and armor:
- Unbevel turns a bevel back into a sharp edge. Unfuse turns a rounded bevel into a flat chamfer, Fuse does the reverse, Change Width resizes it, Select Bevel Strip selects it from one face. Select the bevel faces in Edit Mode first. Meshes imported from a NIF are all triangles: run Face > Triangles to Quads (Alt+J) first.
- Boolean Cut, Join and Intersect with cleanup, and Boolean Cleanup on its own.
- Flatten Normals, Weighted Normals, Transfer Normals, Symmetrize that keeps custom normals, Clear Custom Normals.
- Stashes: automatic backup copies before each edit, saved in the .blend and never exported.
- NIF Vertex Count: the vertex count the NIF will really have, against the 65,535 limit.
- Retopology: Retopologize & Bake, Re-bake from Source, and a button for RetopoFlow.
RetopoFlow (by Orange Turbine, formerly CG Cookie) is free and GPL: download it from its official GitHub releases (version 3.4.10 works in Blender 4.2 to 5.1). MESHmachine is a paid add-on by MACHIN3, sold on its official stores; a GitHub repository offering a free "MESHmachine Windows Download" through an outside password-protected archive (checked 2026-11-05) is a malware lure, not the add-on.

title: Plant shows only its top half (bottom invisible or wireframe) in the Creation Kit or NifSkope after adding wind: Tree flag and vertex alpha
content:
Plant shows only its top half (bottom invisible or wireframe) in the Creation Kit or NifSkope after adding wind: Tree flag and vertex alpha
Fallout 4 wind on plants: the mesh has a BSLeafAnimNode root and stores how much each vertex sways in the vertex colour ALPHA (0 at the base, rising toward the tips). The engine only reads that alpha as sway when the shader says Tree; otherwise vertex alpha is transparency. With an alpha cut-out (for example threshold 128) everything with low sway alpha, which is the bottom of the plant, is cut away.
Two places have to agree:
1. The material file (.bgsm): Tree ticked. Bethesda's swaying plants (KelpAnim01 uses kelp.BGSM, Seaweed01_Tree uses Seaweed01_Tree.BGSM) have it on.
2. The NIF's BSLightingShaderProperty: Shader Flags 2 Tree_Anim ON and Shader Flags 1 Vertex_Alpha OFF. In the 349 vanilla NIFs with a BSLeafAnimNode root, 989 shaders are Tree_Anim on + Vertex_Alpha off (KelpAnim01: flags 0x80400200 / 0x20000031).
Quick fix in NifSkope: select the BSLightingShaderProperty, tick Tree_Anim in Shader Flags 2 (and untick Vertex_Alpha in Shader Flags 1), save. Ticking Tree there made the whole plant show (confirmed 2026-11-09).
Material: do NOT just tick Tree in a material other meshes also use. A rock or cliff sharing it would start using its vertex alpha as sway. Give the windy plant its own copy (for example GSFungusSpore12_Wind.bgsm with Tree on) and point the NIF at it.
Mossy Blender add-on: up to 5.4.9, exporting a wind plant over an existing material kept that material unchanged (Tree off) and kept the imported shader flags, which causes exactly this. The add-on's code now makes the _Wind copy and sets Tree_Anim on / Vertex_Alpha off on export (released in add-on 5.5.1, 2026-11-10).
tags: plant half invisible bottom missing wireframe creation kit nifskope wind vertex alpha tree flag tree_anim vertex_alpha bgsm tree BSLeafAnimNode sway alpha test cutout shared material _Wind.bgsm blender add-on wind
verified_by: GSFungusSpore12.nif exported 2026-11-09 by the add-on: 5,940 of 6,513 vertices with alpha < 128, NiAlphaProperty test 128, shader Vertex_Alpha on / Tree_Anim off, BGSM tree=False; the same BGSM is used by GSDirtCliffLarge01.nif and gloashpile01.nif. Survey of the unpacked game: 349 BSLeafAnimNode NIFs, shader flag counts as quoted; KelpAnim01/Seaweed01_Tree flags read directly. Confirmed on a real setup in NifSkope that ticking Tree shows the whole plant. Add-on fix: local commits 9145a24 and 27a371e (220 tests pass).

title: Making LODs for Fallout 4 objects in the Mossy Blender add-on: one LOD per model, merged models (a cliff with its plants), sharp textures like vanilla, no wind or glow
content:
Making LODs for Fallout 4 objects in the Mossy Blender add-on: one LOD per model, merged models (a cliff with its plants), sharp textures like vanilla, no wind or glow
Fallout 4 object LODs, as the game ships them: files named <Model>_LOD_0.nif, _LOD_1.nif, _LOD_2.nif (1,421 such files in the unpacked game: _LOD_0 1,145, _LOD_1 221, _LOD_2 49, _LOD_3 3, _LOD_FLAT 2; 1,186 of them under Meshes\LOD\).
Vanilla LOD textures (all 529 under Textures\LOD): 256x256 (72%), 128 (22%), 512 (5%), 64 (1%), never 1024; _n and _s always BC5, _d BC1 or BC3 when it has cut-out alpha. They look clear because they are the ORIGINAL textures shrunk, and the LOD meshes keep tiling them (tree trunks use a tiling bark strip, branches use pre-rendered tree cards); one texture set is shared by every LOD level and often by a whole family of models (ElmTrunksLOD, ElmBranchesLOD). A LOD with several kinds of surface has one shape per texture (an elm LOD: trunk shape + branches shape). Of the 160 vanilla LOD materials only 3 have Tree (wind) on and none glow.
One model = one LOD set. A NIF can hold several pieces (GSDirtCliffLarge01.nif is a cliff plus its own grass and spore plants); those pieces belong to ONE model and need ONE LOD set. Separate NIFs (each plant, each rock) each need their own. Delete what is too small to matter at a distance (grass, small plants) before making the LOD.
In the Mossy Blender add-on 5.5.1 (Setup > FO4: LOD + Collision Pipeline):
- LODs for Each Selected Mesh: every selected mesh is its own model and gets its own set, named after the NIF it came from (GSFungusSpore06_LOD_0.nif).
- One LOD for Selected (Merged Model): select all pieces of one model (its collision objects are skipped). A temporary joined copy becomes one LOD set named after the NIF; your pieces are not changed.
- LOD Textures, default 'Original Textures, Shrunk (like vanilla)': every original texture (_d/_n/_s, no glow) is shrunk once to the LOD Texture Size (256/512/1024, default 512) and shared by all three levels; one LOD material per original material (Materials\LOD\...\<Name>LOD.bgsm); each LOD file has one shape per texture. The alternative 'One Baked Texture' bakes the whole model onto one new texture per level, which squeezes a many-times-tiled texture and looks noisier.
- Mesh Sub-path has a folder button: pick ...\YourMod\Meshes\Landscape\Dirtcliffs and only the part after Meshes\ is used.
Problems fixed on the way (all real, 2026-11-09): every face of a decimated many-material LOD got the first material (the plants showed the cliff or grass texture) because clearing the material slots reset the face indices; one-texture bakes looked noisy; 'the LOD only has the plants, the cliff is gone': the Solid Shell method rebuilds the model from voxels and a thin open sheet like a cliff face vanished while chunky plants survived (the copy is now thickened first and the shell must keep at least 80% of the source's surface, so the cliff keeps 100% on every level); the old batch LOD buttons never exported; LODs inherited vertex colours (plant wind alpha cut most of the LOD away), glow flags and the source's collision.
Loose pieces in a LOD are normal when the model itself is made of separate parts: a fungus tree with 39 + 189 separate pieces gave LODs of 39, 27 and 15 pieces, and every LOD piece sat on the real tree's surface (median 2-3 units away, at most 35 units on a 1,400-unit tree). What would be a problem is a piece floating where the full model has nothing; check by measuring each LOD piece's distance to the full model, not by counting pieces.
Cliff missing from the farther LODs of a merged model (a cliff with plants and trees): one Decimate over the whole model removes the cheapest edges first, and a cliff's few big flat triangles are the cheapest, so the cliff collapsed while the dense plants stayed (848 cliff triangles of 14,723: 100, 33, then 2 triangles at LOD1/2/3). The add-on (5.5.2) now decimates each material separately with a share of the budget weighted by surface area and triangle count: the same cliff keeps 489, 163 and 57 triangles at its full size. Generate the LODs again after updating.

title: How Fallout 4 wind (Tree_Anim) moves a mesh, why 3D vines 'breathe' (swell and shrink), and the right wind painting for trees, shrubs, plants, grass, water plants, signs, banners, cloth, nets and sails
content:
How Fallout 4 wind (Tree_Anim) moves a mesh, why 3D vines 'breathe' (swell and shrink), and the right wind painting for trees, shrubs, plants, grass, water plants, signs, banners, cloth, nets and sails
What the game does (the tree wind vertex shader in Shaders011.fxp, read by disassembling it): it reads only the vertex POSITION and the vertex-colour ALPHA. Every vertex moves along ONE horizontal wind direction. The alpha sets how far the vertex moves AND its timing: the sway is a sine of (1 + k x alpha) x a number taken from the object's world position, so two points with different alpha swing out of step. The normal is not used.
Breathing: if alpha changes across the thickness of a 3D part (a vine, a stem), its sides move different amounts and at different times, so the part swells and shrinks. Even small alpha steps ALONG a thick vine make it stretch. Bethesda avoids this: in DLC04 Briar_BushM01 the lower half or more of each thick vine is exactly 0 and only the tip moves; flat leaf cards carry one value per card.
Vanilla rules (1,256 wind shapes in 479 NIFs, PreCombined/LOD excluded): 94% of Tree_Anim shapes have vertex colours (1,278 of 1,359 in a full scan); the root is BSLeafAnimNode (998) or NiNode (257); the BGSM has Tree on (1,222 of 1,240); Vertex_Alpha is off (1,171); RGB is white (1,128) or a tint. Pieces start at 0 where they attach (89%).
Strongest wind (alpha out of 255) and how it rises along each piece, by type: tree 255, rises early (about t^0.7); shrub/bush about 185, mostly at the tip (t^2.5, the lower 40% barely moves); plant about 130, steadily; grass about 155, whole blade; water plants (kelp, coral, reeds) about 127, only the end (t^3); hanging sign 255, hangs from its top edge; banner/flag 161, cloth/tent/tablecloth 255, net 200, sail 50, all growing with distance from the fastened points; windmills 0 (they are animated, not wind).
In the Mossy Blender add-on (Wind Animation > Vegetation Wind (Vertex Groups)): Wind Type (Auto picks it from the object name, then the material name); each connected piece is painted along its own length and kept the same across its thickness, with the vanilla curve for its type. For cloth, banners, nets and sails make a vertex group named WindPin with the fastened vertices; without it the top edge stays still. Keep Wind From: pick the original game NIF a mesh was made from and every vertex still where the original had one keeps Bethesda's exact alpha; only new parts are painted by the rules. That is the real fix for a vanilla-based plant whose thick vines breathe. Smart Wind Setup (Auto) skips signs and cloth (they count as static).
tags: wind tree_anim breathing vines swell shrink expand 3D vine stem vertex alpha vertex colour sway BSLeafAnimNode wind shader per piece shrub bush plant grass kelp coral sign banner flag cloth tent tarp net sail WindPin keep wind from original nif vegetation wind setup wind type
verified_by: Wind shader: Shaders011.fxp vertex shaders disassembled with D3DDisassemble (55 of 1,339 read COLOR alpha + sincos). Vanilla scan 2026-11-10 of 1,256 Tree_Anim shapes plus a full PyNifly scan (1,359 Tree_Anim shapes, 1,278 with vertex colours). Curves measured per type over every moving piece. A real vanilla-based bush (Briar_BushM01 geometry plus a leaf card) breathed in game with rule painting and its thick vines still moved with per-type curves; with Keep Wind From the export matched vanilla alpha on 383 of 383 vertices. Add-on repaint of 12 vanilla meshes: right type for all, max alpha within the vanilla range, cross-section spread 0-2.

title: Exported NIF is 0 bytes / 'could not open as nif' after an export that said it succeeded: the drive is full
content:
Exported NIF is 0 bytes / 'could not open as nif' after an export that said it succeeded: the drive is full
If a NIF you just exported is EMPTY (0 bytes) and tools then say they could not open it as a NIF, check the free space on the drive you exported to first. On a full drive Windows creates the file but nothing can be written into it, and the exporter (PyNifly) still reports success. A 0-byte NIF will not load in NifSkope or the Creation Kit and can break the cell in game that uses it.
Fix: free space on that drive (large downloads such as a Steam game, the Recycle Bin, repacked archive mods are the usual suspects), then export again. The Mossy Blender add-on now reports a 0-byte export as a failed export and shows the drive's free space.
tags: nif 0 bytes empty file export failed could not open as nif disk full drive full no space left export says successfully pynifly nifskope can't open
verified_by: Real case 2026-11-10: an export to a mod folder produced a 0-byte NIF while PyNifly printed 'completed SUCCESSFULLY'; the drive had 0.00 GB free (a 91 GB game download in progress). The same export to a drive with space produced a normal 12 KB NIF.

title: How Fallout 4 animation is wired: race -> behavior project -> behavior graphs -> clips (.hkx) -> skeleton, plus idle records, movement types and animation events
content:
How Fallout 4 animation is wired: race -> behavior project -> behavior graphs -> clips (.hkx) -> skeleton, plus idle records, movement types and animation events
Chain for every NPC and creature: the RACE record names the skeleton (Actors\<Creature>\CharacterAssets\skeleton.nif, with a matching skeleton.hkx holding the Havok skeleton and ragdoll) and the behavior project (for example Actors\FeralGhoul\FeralGhoulProject.hkx, Actors\Character\RaiderProject.hkx). The project loads behavior graphs (Behaviors\*.hkx: state machines, blend trees, events, variables); their clip generators point at clips under Animations\ (written as .hkt in the graph, shipped as .hkx). The race also lists attack events (ATKE, e.g. meleeStart_Bite1) and default movement types (MOVT: walk/run speeds per direction); IDLE records play an animation event in a named behavior graph (3,703 idles; furniture, dialogue, flavor).
Clips: Havok 2014 64-bit packfiles, spline-compressed, 30 fps (14,679 vanilla clips; a few pose clips use 3 fps), bound to a skeleton by name (the main skeleton is usually called 'Root'). Locomotion clips carry root motion (extracted motion) - the distance it covers per second should match the race's movement type, or feet slide. Some clips are additive (layered on top: leaning, injured limbs).
Clip play modes in behavior graphs: 0 = play once (deaths, exits), 1 = loop (idles, locomotion), 2 = user controlled.
Animation events (annotations) and where they sit in a clip (median position, 0 = start, 1 = end): FootLeft 0.54 / FootRight 0.45 (and FootFront/FootBack for four-legged creatures) for footstep sounds and IK; SyncLeft/SyncRight for blending gaits; preHitFrame 0.25, weaponSwing 0.23, HitFrame 0.38 for melee (the hit lands at HitFrame); weaponFire 0.46 (weaponFire.0..4 for multi-weapon creatures); SoundPlay.<sound> for sounds (0.18); startAllowRotation, startAnimationDriven, attackStop 0.9, attackWinStart/End for combo windows; CameraShake.<a,b,c>; PathTweenerStart/End; HeadTrackingOff/On; reloadComplete 0.65 / reloadEnd 0.89; PairEnd/pairedStop 0.96 for paired kills.

title: Fallout 4 creature and NPC animation reference: skeleton bones, clip counts, movement speeds and attack events per creature
content:
Fallout 4 creature and NPC animation reference: skeleton bones, clip counts, movement speeds and attack events per creature
Vanilla numbers per creature (main skeleton bones / ragdoll bones; clips; default movement type forward walk / run in units per second; race attack events):
- Human (HumanRace, RaiderProject): 201 bones / 18; 7,486 clips (idles 1,556, furniture 1,217, walk 970, weapon 885, run 708, turns 465, hits 322, attacks 257, paired 161); measured walk about 63, run about 239, sprint 500; 26 attack events; 1,412 idle records.
- Power armor: 110 / 15; 1,861 clips; walk about 102, run 301, sprint 497.
- Super mutant: 93 / 17; 799 clips; 27 attack events. Behemoth: 79 / 19; Behemoth_Default_MT 98 / 300.
- Feral ghoul: 91 / 18; 148 clips (hits 55); FeralGhoul_Default_MT 53 / 300; 21 attack events (meleeStart_...); 82 idles.
- Deathclaw: 86 / 28; 176 clips; Deathclaw_Default_MT 133 / 520; 9 attack events (meleeAttackStartPowerHornRam, ...).
- Dogmeat: 65 / 24; 443 clips (turns 132, sneak 45, paired 23); 4 attack events; 312 idles.
- Radstag 57 / 31, RadStag_Default_MT 58 / 500; Yao guai 83 / 18; Mirelurk 70 / 23 (60.7 / 425); Mirelurk king 90 / 22 (195 / 360); Molerat 39 / 20; Radscorpion 74 / 49; Brahmin 47 / 39; Bloatfly 46 / 23; Bloodbug 31 / 23; Mongrel/FEV hound 52 / 22; Assaultron 112 bones (100 / 400); Sentry bot (100 / 300); Fog crawler 87 / 65 (118 / 443).
Every creature's full bone list, clip list with durations and events, behavior events/variables and race links is in the animation catalog (anim_creatures.json).

title: Making custom animations for a Fallout 4 NPC or creature: what a new clip must match to work in game
content:
Making custom animations for a Fallout 4 NPC or creature: what a new clip must match to work in game
Checklist taken from how all vanilla clips are built:
1. Skeleton: animate on the creature's own skeleton with exactly its bone names and hierarchy (for example the feral ghoul has 91 bones starting Root, buffer, COM, Pelvis, LThigh...). The clip binds to the skeleton by name; missing or renamed bones do not move.
2. Format: Havok 2014 64-bit packfile, 30 fps, spline compressed (what the Creation Kit / Havok tools and community converters produce for FO4). Keep the bind pose the same as the skeleton's reference pose.
3. Root motion: walk/run/turn clips must carry root motion, and its speed should match the race's movement type (feral ghoul 53 walk / 300 run), or the feet slide.
4. Events: add the annotations the behavior and game expect - FootLeft/FootRight (or FootFront/FootBack) on each footfall, SyncLeft/SyncRight on loops, preHitFrame then HitFrame for melee (HitFrame is when damage lands), weaponSwing, SoundPlay.<sound> for sounds, attackStop near the end. Without HitFrame a melee attack does no damage.
5. Hooking it up: the simplest route is replacing an existing clip with the same file name and similar length (no behavior edit). A new clip needs a clip generator in the creature's behavior graph (or an existing generator pointed at it), and idles need an IDLE record that names the behavior graph and the animation event. Attacks are triggered by the race's attack events (ATKE).
6. Loop or once: idles and locomotion loop (play mode 1); attacks, deaths, get-ups play once (mode 0).
